subject: SCCs alignment + Order Form risk-ladder & DPA asks
messages:
From: Marta Garcia <marta.garcia@solarahealth.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-04T08:12:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Revised Order Form and DPA redlines

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for sending over the updated order form and the DPA redlines yesterday. We did a first-pass here at Solara and have three areas where we need clarification before we can move to legal sign-off:

1) SCCs substitution: you replaced the standard EU SCCs with a vendor-specific annex. We need confirmation that the annex contains the equivalent protections and that you will sign the standard SCCs if regulators request.

2) Role mapping and subprocessor disclosures: the order form still lists processor vs controller roles in a way that is ambiguous for our data flows. We need an explicit controller/processor statement for (i) analytics telemetry, (ii) hosted inference logs, and (iii) embeddings indexing.

3) Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA): given the hosting footprint you shared (EU primary + fallback in us-east1), our counsel wants a TIA with a short remediation commitment if a supervisory authority flags an issue.

Attached our consolidated redlines: Solara_DPA_Redlines_20270503.pdf (PDF, 12 pages).

We can be flexible on liability caps if the data residency and TIA language are solid. Can your team propose a prioritized list of the asks (critical vs negotiable)? Also, we have a procurement window this quarter and would prefer to close next week if possible.

Best,

Marta Garcia
Head of Procurement
Solara Health
-----
Attachment: Solara_DPA_Redlines_20270503.pdf (redlines PDF)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: marta.garcia@solarahealth.com
Date: 2027-05-04T10:05:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Revised Order Form and DPA redlines

Laura / Ben / Monica — looping you in from Legal / Privacy / Sales Ops.

Summary of Solara's asks (I extracted these from Marta's attachment):
- SCC substitution confirmation (customer prefers standard SCCs or clear equivalence) — customer note: regulatory fallback required.
- Explicit role map for three data flows (analytics telemetry, inference logs, embeddings index).
- TIA + remediation commitment window.
- Conditional appetite to adjust cap if residency/TIA satisfied.

I've drafted a simple prioritization (attached): Redwood_OrderForm_Risk_Ladder_v1.xlsx. High-level proposal:

Critical (must resolve before signature)
- SCC equivalence or standard SCC signature fallback.
- Role mapping clarification for inference logs (we'll be processor for inference requests, controller for customer-provided training data only).

High (resolve in parallel, can't be indefinite)
- TIA scope and remediation SLA (we propose a 30-day remediation window with quarterly review).
- Subprocessor disclosure cadence (monthly portal vs on-demand).

Medium (commercial concessions to trade)
- Liability cap adjustments (we can offer limited increases tied to verified SOC2 + TIA completion).

Low (nice-to-have)
- Data localization voucher / optional dedicated pool (pricing impact).

Ask for Legal: can you sign off on the SCC fallback language proposed in tab \"SCC-fallback\" of the risk ladder file? Also see suggested language in the \"TIA\" tab. If legal is ok, I'll send a short memo to Solara that states Redwood will: (1) accept standard SCCs on regulator request; (2) deliver a TIA within 14 business days after signature and commit to remediation timelines.

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura to confirm SCC fallback text and whether it triggers exec escalation.
2) Ben to prepare a concise commercial fallback offer tied to SOC2 evidence.
3) Monica to confirm operational feasibility for a 30-day remediation window.

I put a meeting on for Thursday (15:30 CET) to walk through if that helps — link in the Drive (see related_links).

Cheers,
Rafael
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
redwood.com
-----
Attachment: Redwood_OrderForm_Risk_Ladder_v1.xlsx (Excel, 3 sheets: \"Risk Ladder\", \"SCC-fallback\", \"TIA\")

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, marta.garcia@solarahealth.com
Date: 2027-05-04T13:12:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Revised Order Form and DPA redlines

Thanks for the clear summary, Rafael — good framing. A few points from Legal & Privacy after a quick review:

1) SCCs / Annex: we can accept the vendor annex as long as it is certified to contain the full protections of the 2021 SCCs and we include an "SCCs on request" fallback clause. Recommended language (redline attached) adds a single sentence in the DPA: \"If a competent supervisory authority or customer requires the execution of the EU Commission's standard contractual clauses, Redwood will execute the applicable SCCs within 10 business days and the annex shall be considered their binding supplement.\" See redline_language_sccs.docx.

2) Role mapping: I'm attaching a short exhibit template that explicitly states controller | processor responsibilities for each flow. For the three flows Rafael listed: (i) analytics telemetry — processor; (ii) hosted inference logs — processor (transient logs retained up to 30 days, see retention table); (iii) embeddings index — processor, but customer can opt-out of indexing. We'll add the table to the Order Form as Exhibit A.

3) TIA: Legal wants the TIA to be delivered pre-signature when Solara flags it as a hard requirement. If we cannot deliver it pre-signature, we can offer to complete a scoped TIA within 14 business days post-signature with a remediation commitment (30 days for mitigation steps, 90 days for full remediation). Operationally reasonable?

4) Liability & cap: we generally won't raise the cap beyond 2x annual contract value. If Solara provides recent SOC2 + penetration test report and accepts the TIA timeline above, we can add a limited cap carveout tied to indemnity for breach of security obligations. Ben, please confirm commercial appetite and any precedent.

5) Escalation: if the customer insists on full data localization wording, we will need exec approval (pricing + infra booking).

I attached the redline document with our recommended language and the exhibit template for role mapping. If everyone is aligned I'll prepare the short memo for Solara and propose a single consolidated DPA redline to minimize churn.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
-----
Attachment: redline_language_sccs.docx (Word doc, includes proposed single-sentence fallback + exhibit template)
From: Marta Garcia <marta.garcia@solarahealth.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-04T16:03:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Revised Order Form and DPA redlines

Thanks — this is helpful and quick. We appreciate the "SCCs on request" fallback language; that addresses the bulk of our regulator concern. A couple quick points:

- Solara's legal would still prefer to see the full TIA before signature if it's materially different than the standard annex language. If Redwood needs the signature first, we can accept the 14-business-day TIA commitment, but we'll reserve the right to pause data flows if material issues are discovered.

- For role mapping: the Exhibit A template looks good, please ensure we have an explicit opt-out checkbox for embeddings indexing (our privacy team will require it).

- Commercial: we are happy to provide SOC2 evidence within two business days. On liability cap: we prefer to negotiate to 3x ACV for the first year and then revert to 2x thereafter. Would Redwood be comfortable with a year-1 uplift if SOC2 + TIA are in place?

We can do a short call tomorrow 10:00-10:30 CET to finalize the path. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and include a DocuSign pointer to the existing MSA for reference: https://docusign.com/link/abc123-msaign

Best,
Marta
